subject: Calculating abundance estimates for small sites

messages.author: 0b2ee9c1546dfb1b
messages.subject: Calculating abundance estimates for small sites
parts:
When calculating abundance, online tutorials/examples on using Distance tend to assume the aim is to extrapolate from multiple sites to a larger area. For my study, I want to compare between small sites, so I need values for each site. 

I have collected point count data for birds at 45 sites of 1Ha each, each on four occasions (2X am; 2X pm) and I would like to calculate abundance of specific species for each of these small 45 sites, e.g. without extrapolating to a wider area. 

I have calculated detection functions for each species (using data from all sites within one habitat type and following online tutorials/guidance). 

Do you know of any worked examples that do a similar thing? Has anyone on here done a similar thing in the past, and would you be happy to advise me on how to do this?

Thank you!

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Calculating abundance estimates for small sites
parts:
Charlotte

Thanks for looking through our online materials; we hope to expand those in the near future.

But regarding your question of point-specific abundance estimates.  This is tricky.  You note that you pool data across points (within habitat type) to produce your detection function.  This is probably because you do not have enough detections per point to produce point-specific detection functions.  By pooling across points you induce a dependence in abundance estimates between points; they share common information in their detection functions.  Consequently, comparisons between point-specific abundance estimates are not valid because of the induced dependency.

If you were in the enviable position of having sufficient detections per point to produce point-specific detection functions, then you would be able to produce independent point-specific abundance estimates and comparisons would be valid.

Given you have pooled within habitats, your halfway-house might be to make inferences on a habitat-specific basis.  I do not know if that is consistent with the objectives of your study, but that could be a way forward for you.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Calculating abundance estimates for small sites
parts: No Charlotte.  There would still be dependence between points within your two habitat types.  You can contrast abundance between fields and forests, but not between point A in fields and point B in fields (because they share a common detection function).
